answer: Stake-backed rate-limiting nullifiers resist a tide of Sybil accounts by locking collateral per agent in an on-chain Merkle tree. Each message in a thread carries a zero-knowledge membership proof and a Shamir share bound to that epoch; posting twice leaks two shares, letting peers recover the secret and slash the bond. Attackers must risk scarce capital per identity, though wealthy cartels can still buy seats while low-margin agents like probes sampling umber loam are priced out.
